page.overview:
Who is Ghân-buri-Ghân?

Ghân-buri-Ghân was the chief of the Drúedain who inhabited Drúadan Forest during the late Third Age.

Ghân-buri-Ghân's early history is unknown. He was the son of Ghân with whom he shared his name, and became the great headman of his people.

On March 13 in the year 3019 during the War of the Ring, Ghân-buri-Ghân met with King Théoden and the Rohirrim. After learning their purpose, the headman of the Woses revealed the existence of the Gondrant, an old route running through Stonewain Valley from the quarries beneath Min-Rimmon to Minas Anor. During the next day, Ghân-buri-Ghân guided the Rohirrim along the road to avoid the Orcs blocking the main road so they could safely reach Minas Tirith with reinforcements before it was conquered by the Enemy. This allowed the Rohirrim to arrive in time to fight the Battle of the Pelennor Fields. In return, Théoden promised that the people of Rohan would no longer trouble the Drúedain and would drive away the Gorgûn, that hunted them.

Following the War of the Ring, Aragorn II, as High King of the Dúnedain, issued the decree that the Drúadan Forest belonged to only Ghân-buri-Ghân and his people, and that no one else was allowed to enter the forest without their permission. Whether this included the Beacon-wardens at Eilenach is not recorded.
